name: Congenital Pulmonary Sequestration

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Radiologic and Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Pulmonary Sequestration

criteria.description: Presence of an aberrant systemic arterial supply to the sequestered lung tissue
Identification of nonfunctioning lung tissue lacking normal bronchial connection
Imaging evidence (CT angiography or MRI) showing sequestered lung segment and anomalous vasculature
Recurrent localized pulmonary infections or respiratory distress in infancy or childhood

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of aberrant systemic arterial supply and imaging confirmation of sequestered lung tissue without normal bronchial connection
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Definitive diagnosis relies primarily on imaging and vascular anatomy demonstration.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Aberrant systemic arterial supply to lung tissue
pathognomonic.notes: Identified via imaging; hallmark of sequestration

pathognomonic.symptomName: Nonfunctioning pulmonary segment lacking bronchial connection
searchTerms: lung segment not connected to airways
repeated lung infections in same area

common.symptomName: Respiratory distress in infancy or early childhood
searchTerms: breathing problems in infancy or early childhood

common.symptomName: Wheezing localized to affected lung area
searchTerms: wheezing sound in affected lung area

occasional.symptomName: Chest pain localized to sequestration site

searchTerms: failure to gain weight as expected
high blood pressure in lungs due to lesion

laboratory: Non-specific inflammatory markers elevated during infection episodes
Normal routine blood counts outside infection
imaging: CT angiography showing aberrant systemic arterial supply
MRI demonstrating sequestered lung segment without bronchial communication
Chest X-ray revealing localized opacity or cystic lesion
genetic: No known specific genetic mutations associated
other: Surgical pathology confirming nonfunctioning lung tissue without normal bronchial connections

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of cystic lung lesions with normal pulmonary arterial supply
Isolated cystic lesion without aberrant systemic blood supply
No recurrent infections typical of sequestration

redFlags: Severe recurrent pulmonary infections unresponsive to standard treatment
Respiratory failure or severe distress in infancy
references: Stocker JT. Congenital pulmonary airway malformations and related lesions. Semin Diagn Pathol. 2012.
Savic B, Birtel FJ, Tholen W, Funke HD, Knoche R. Lung sequestration: report of seven cases and review of 540 published cases. Thorax. 1979.
Corbett HJ, Humphrey GM. Pulmonary sequestration. Paediatr Respir Rev. 2004.
